formulas.title: The Pythagorean Theorem
formulas.description: Defines the fundamental relationship between the sides of a right triangle in Euclidean geometry, serving as the basis for distance metrics, Euclidean vectors, and trigonometry.

formulas.title: Euler's Identity
formulas.description: Widely celebrated as one of the most beautiful equations in mathematics, it unifies the five fundamental constants ($e$, $i$, $\pi$, $1$, and $0$) using addition, multiplication, and exponentiation.

formulas.title: Euler's Formula
formulas.description: Establishes the fundamental bridge between trigonometric functions and complex exponential functions, underpinning signal processing and Fourier analysis.

formulas.title: The Quadratic Formula
formulas.description: Provides the exact analytical solution to the roots of any quadratic equation of the form $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$.

formulas.title: The Binomial Theorem
formulas.description: Describes the algebraic expansion of powers of a binomial sum into a series using binomial coefficients.

formulas.title: Euler’s Polyhedral Formula
formulas.description: Relates the number of vertices ($V$), edges ($E$), and faces ($F$) of any convex polyhedron, forming the foundation of combinatorial topology.

formulas.title: The Law of Cosines
formulas.description: Generalizes the Pythagorean theorem to any arbitrary triangle, relating side lengths to the cosine of one of the angles.

formulas.title: The Law of Sines
formulas.description: Relates the sides of an arbitrary triangle to the sines of their opposing angles and the radius $R$ of its circumscribed circle.

formulas.title: Heron's Formula
formulas.description: Calculates the area ($A$) of any triangle from its three side lengths ($a, b, c$), where $s = \frac{a+b+c}{2}$ is the semi-perimeter.

formulas.title: The Prime Number Theorem
formulas.description: Describes the asymptotic distribution of prime numbers among positive integers, stating that the number of primes less than $x$ approaches $x/\ln x$ as $x \to \infty$.

formulas.title: The Basel Problem (Euler's Sum)
formulas.description: Solved by Leonhard Euler in 1734, revealing an unexpected connection between reciprocal squares of integers and $\pi$.

formulas.title: The Riemann Zeta Function
formulas.description: Relates the summation over all integers to the Euler product over all prime numbers, central to modern analytic number theory.

formulas.title: De Moivre’s Formula
formulas.description: Allows powers of complex numbers in polar form to be computed directly via angle multiplication.

formulas.title: Stirling's Approximation
formulas.description: Provides an asymptotic estimate for factorials of large numbers, essential in combinatorics and statistical physics.

formulas.title: The Chudnovsky Algorithm for $\pi$
formulas.description: An ultra-fast converging hypergeometric series used by modern supercomputers to compute trillions of digits of $\pi$.

formulas.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
formulas.description: Links differentiation and definite integration as inverse operations, enabling the analytical calculation of accumulated areas and quantities.

formulas.title: The Formal Definition of the Derivative
formulas.description: Defines the instantaneous rate of change of a continuous function at a given point as the limit of a difference quotient.

formulas.title: Integration by Parts
formulas.description: Derived from the product rule of differentiation, allowing the integration of products of functions.

formulas.title: Taylor Series Expansion
formulas.description: Represents any infinitely differentiable function as an infinite polynomial expansion evaluated around a reference point $a$.

formulas.title: The Continuous Fourier Transform
formulas.description: Decomposes a time-domain or spatial-domain function into its constituent frequency components.

formulas.title: The Inverse Fourier Transform
formulas.description: Reconstructs the original time-domain function from its continuous frequency spectrum.

formulas.title: The Laplace Transform
formulas.description: Transforms linear ordinary differential equations in the time domain into simpler algebraic equations in the complex frequency domain.

formulas.title: The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
formulas.description: A foundational inequality in linear algebra and functional analysis bounding the inner product of two vectors by their norms.

formulas.title: Cauchy's Integral Formula
formulas.description: Shows that for a holomorphic complex function, its value inside a closed contour is completely determined by values on the boundary.

formulas.title: Cauchy's Residue Theorem
formulas.description: A powerful contour integration tool that evaluates complex line integrals by calculating local residues at interior singularities.

formulas.title: The Divergence (Gauss-Ostrogradsky) Theorem
formulas.description: Relates the volume integral of the divergence of a vector field to the surface flux through its closed boundary.

formulas.title: Stokes' Theorem
formulas.description: Relates the surface integral of the curl of a vector field over an open surface to the circulation along the boundary curve.

formulas.title: Green’s Theorem
formulas.latex: \oint_C (L\,dx + M\,dy) = \iint_D \left(\frac{\partial M}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial L}{\partial y}\right) dA
formulas.description: A two-dimensional special case of Stokes' theorem relating line integrals around a plane curve to double integrals over the enclosed region.

formulas.title: The Heat Equation
formulas.description: A parabolic partial differential equation governing the diffusion of thermal energy and passive particles over time.

formulas.title: The Classical Wave Equation
formulas.description: A hyperbolic partial differential equation describing the propagation of mechanical, acoustic, and electromagnetic waves through a medium at speed $v$.

formulas.title: Bayes' Theorem
formulas.description: Calculates conditional probability by updating the prior belief $P(A)$ in light of observed evidence $B$.

formulas.title: The Normal (Gaussian) Distribution
formulas.description: Defines the symmetric bell-shaped probability density function with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

formulas.title: The Central Limit Theorem
formulas.description: States that the normalized sum of independent and identically distributed random variables tends toward a standard normal distribution.

formulas.title: The Poisson Distribution
formulas.description: Models the probability of $k$ independent events occurring within a fixed interval given a known average rate $\lambda$.

formulas.title: The Binomial Distribution
formulas.description: Calculates the probability of observing exactly $k$ successes out of $n$ independent Bernoulli trials with probability $p$.

formulas.title: Variance of a Random Variable
formulas.description: Measures the dispersion or spread of values of a random variable around its mathematical expectation $\mu$.

formulas.title: Covariance
formulas.description: Quantifies the joint directional variability of two distinct random variables.

formulas.title: Pearson Correlation Coefficient
formulas.description: Measures the strength and direction of linear association between two variables, normalized between $-1$ and $+1$.

formulas.title: Shannon Entropy
formulas.description: Quantifies the fundamental limit of expected information content, uncertainty, and lossless compression rate for a discrete source.

formulas.title: Kullback-Leibler Divergence
formulas.description: Measures the relative statistical distance and information loss when approximating true distribution $P$ with reference distribution $Q$.

formulas.title: Chebyshev's Inequality
formulas.description: Guarantees an upper bound on the probability that a random variable deviates by more than $k$ standard deviations from the mean.

formulas.title: Weak Law of Large Numbers
formulas.description: States that the sample average of independent trials converges in probability toward the theoretical population mean $\mu$.

formulas.title: The Black-Scholes Equation
formulas.latex: \frac{\partial V}{\partial t} + \frac{1}{2}\sigma^2 S^2 \frac{\partial^2 V}{\partial S^2} + rS \frac{\partial V}{\partial S} - rV = 0
formulas.description: A partial differential equation modeling the fair financial pricing of European derivative options over time.

formulas.title: Newton's Second Law of Motion
formulas.description: Relates net applied force ($\mathbf{F}$) to the time rate of change of linear momentum ($\mathbf{p}$), or mass times acceleration for invariant mass.

formulas.title: Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation
formulas.description: Describes the inverse-square gravitational attraction between two point masses separated by distance $r$.

formulas.title: Kinetic Energy
formulas.description: Quantifies the mechanical work stored in an object of mass $m$ by virtue of its velocity $v$ or momentum $p$.

formulas.title: Gravitational Potential Energy (Uniform Field)
formulas.description: Measures potential energy gained by lifting mass $m$ to height $h$ in a uniform gravitational field $g$.

formulas.title: General Gravitational Potential Energy
formulas.description: Describes the potential energy of a two-body system separated by distance $r$, set to zero at infinite separation.

formulas.title: Hooke's Law
formulas.description: Models linear restoring force exerted by an ideal spring stretched or compressed by displacement $x$.

formulas.title: Simple Harmonic Angular Frequency
formulas.description: Defines the natural angular frequency of oscillation for an undamped mass-spring oscillator.

formulas.title: Period of a Simple Pendulum
formulas.description: Approximates the small-amplitude period of oscillation for a pendulum of length $L$ in gravitational field $g$.

formulas.title: Kepler's Third Law (Harmonic Law)
formulas.description: Relates orbital period ($T$) squared to semi-major axis ($a$) cubed for elliptical orbits around a central mass.

formulas.title: The Work-Energy Theorem
formulas.description: Demonstrates that the net work done by all forces on a body equals the net change in its kinetic energy.

formulas.title: The Euler-Lagrange Equation
formulas.description: Forms the cornerstone of analytical Lagrangian mechanics, identifying paths of stationary action for generalized coordinates $q_i$.

formulas.title: Hamilton's Canonical Equations
formulas.description: Replaces second-order Lagrangian equations with a coupled set of first-order differential equations in phase space $(q, p)$.

formulas.title: The First Law of Thermodynamics
formulas.description: Expresses conservation of energy: internal energy change ($dU$) equals heat added ($\delta Q$) minus thermodynamic work done ($\delta W$).

formulas.title: The Second Law of Thermodynamics (Clausius Inequality)
formulas.description: States that the entropy ($S$) of an isolated physical system never decreases over time during spontaneous processes.

formulas.title: Boltzmann’s Entropy Formula
formulas.description: Bridges microscopic states and macroscopic thermodynamics, connecting thermodynamic entropy to the number of microstates $\Omega$.

formulas.title: The Ideal Gas Law
formulas.description: Equation of state describing an idealized non-interacting gas in terms of pressure, volume, temperature, and substance quantity.

formulas.title: Carnot Engine Thermal Efficiency
formulas.description: Sets the theoretical maximum reversible thermodynamic efficiency for any heat engine operating between hot ($T_H$) and cold ($T_C$) reservoirs.

formulas.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann Speed Distribution
formulas.description: Gives the statistical probability density of molecular speeds for an ideal gas at thermodynamic temperature $T$.

formulas.title: Gibbs Free Energy
formulas.description: Thermodynamic potential used to predict chemical reaction spontaneity and equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure.

formulas.title: Enthalpy Definition
formulas.description: Quantifies the total heat content of a thermodynamic system, incorporating internal energy ($U$) and flow work ($PV$).

formulas.title: The Stefan-Boltzmann Law
formulas.description: States that total radiant energy emitted per unit surface area of a blackbody is proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature.

formulas.title: Planck’s Law of Blackbody Radiation
formulas.description: Accurately predicts spectral radiation density without the classical ultraviolet catastrophe, initiating quantum mechanics.

formulas.title: Gauss's Law (Electrostatics)
formulas.description: States that the divergence of the electric field equals local volume charge density divided by vacuum permittivity.

formulas.title: Gauss's Law for Magnetism
formulas.description: Expresses the non-existence of isolated magnetic monopoles; magnetic field lines form continuous closed loops.

formulas.title: Faraday’s Law of Electromagnetic Induction
formulas.description: States that a time-varying magnetic field induces a spatially circulating non-conservative electric field.

formulas.title: The Ampère-Maxwell Law
formulas.description: Shows that magnetic fields are produced by conduction current densities ($\mathbf{J}$) and Maxwell's displacement currents.

formulas.title: The Lorentz Force Law
formulas.description: Calculates the total electromagnetic force acting on a particle carrying electric charge $q$ moving with velocity $\mathbf{v}$.

formulas.title: Coulomb’s Law
formulas.description: Quantifies the electrostatic force between two stationary electric point charges separated by distance $r$.

formulas.title: Ohm's Law (Microscopic and Macroscopic)
formulas.description: Relates electric potential difference ($V$) across a conductor to current ($I$) and electrical resistance ($R$).

formulas.title: Snell’s Law of Refraction
formulas.description: Describes the angular bending of light rays passing across the interface between two media of differing refractive indices.

formulas.title: The Poynting Vector
formulas.description: Represents the directional energy flux density (power per unit area) transported by an electromagnetic wave.

formulas.title: Speed of Light from Electromagnetic Constants
formulas.description: Directly proves that light is an electromagnetic wave whose speed is fixed by electric permittivity and magnetic permeability.

formulas.title: Mass-Energy Equivalence
formulas.description: Asserts that mass and rest energy are directly proportional and interchangeable via the speed of light squared.

formulas.title: Relativistic Energy-Momentum Relation
formulas.description: Calculates total relativistic energy ($E$) for particles with rest mass $m_0$ and momentum $p$, including massless photons ($E = pc$).

formulas.title: The Lorentz Factor
formulas.description: Dimensionless scale factor by which time, length, and relativistic mass scale as relative speed $v$ approaches $c$.

formulas.title: Relativistic Time Dilation
formulas.description: Shows that a clock moving at speed $v$ ticks slower relative to a stationary observer's reference frame.

formulas.title: Relativistic Length Contraction
formulas.description: Demonstrates that the physical length of an object appears contracted along its direction of travel at relativistic speeds.

formulas.title: Einstein's Field Equations of General Relativity
formulas.description: Relates the geometry and curvature of spacetime ($G_{\mu\nu}$) to the distribution of matter and energy ($T_{\mu\nu}$).

formulas.title: The Schwarzschild Radius
formulas.description: Calculates the radius defining the event horizon of a non-rotating spherically symmetric black hole of mass $M$.

formulas.title: The Spacetime Invariant Interval
formulas.description: Defines the invariant distance between two events in flat Minkowski spacetime, invariant across all inertial reference frames.

formulas.title: The Planck-Einstein Relation
formulas.description: States that the energy of a photon is directly quantized in discrete packets proportional to its electromagnetic frequency.

formulas.title: The de Broglie Wavelength
formulas.description: Establishes wave-particle duality, showing that every moving physical particle with momentum $p$ possesses a characteristic wavelength.

formulas.title: The Time-Dependent Schrödinger Equation
formulas.description: Governs the deterministic evolution of the quantum wave function $\Psi$ over time under Hamiltonian operator $\hat{H}$.

formulas.title: The Time-Independent Schrödinger Equation
formulas.description: An eigenvalue problem determining stationary quantum energy states ($E$) and spatial wavefunctions ($\psi$).

formulas.title: Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle
formulas.description: Sets the fundamental quantum mechanical bound on the simultaneous measurement precision of position and momentum.

formulas.title: The Dirac Equation
formulas.description: Unifies quantum mechanics with special relativity for spin-$1/2$ fermions, predicting antimatter and intrinsic spin.

formulas.title: Bohr Orbit Radius
formulas.description: Calculates the quantized radius of stable electron orbits in hydrogen-like atoms for principal quantum number $n$.

formulas.title: The Rydberg Formula
formulas.description: Predicts wavelengths of spectral emission lines caused by electron transitions between discrete energy shells in hydrogen.

formulas.title: The Fermi-Dirac Distribution
formulas.description: Describes statistical energy level occupation for identical fermions obeying the Pauli exclusion principle.

formulas.title: The Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
formulas.description: Governs the momentum conservation and fluid motion for viscous, incompressible Newtonian fluid flows.

formulas.title: The Fluid Continuity Equation
formulas.description: Expresses the local conservation of mass within a continuous fluid or compressible medium.

formulas.title: Bernoulli's Principle
formulas.description: Expresses conservation of mechanical energy along a streamline for steady, frictionless, incompressible fluid flow.

formulas.title: The Arrhenius Equation
formulas.description: Models the temperature dependence of chemical reaction rate constants based on activation energy $E_a$.

formulas.title: The Nernst Equation
formulas.description: Determines the equilibrium reduction potential of an electrochemical cell as a function of temperature and reaction quotient $Q$.

formulas.title: The Hubble-Lemaître Law
formulas.description: Describes the cosmological expansion of the universe, relating recessional velocity ($v$) of galaxies to physical distance ($d$).

formulas.title: The First Friedmann Equation
formulas.description: Derives the expansion rate of homogeneous, isotropic universes from general relativity, where $a(t)$ is the scale factor.

formulas.title: The Logistic Map
formulas.description: A canonical nonlinear polynomial mapping exhibiting period-doubling routes to deterministic chaos in dynamic systems.
